# Welcome! {background-color="#43464B"}

## Workshop Overview {.smaller}

**Duration:** 2 hours

**What we'll cover:**

- Session 1 (50 min): Quarto Basics & Document Creation
- Break (10 min)
- Session 2 (60 min): Advanced Features & Real-World Applications

**Prerequisites:**

- RStudio or VS Code installed
- Quarto installed ([quarto.org](https://quarto.org))
- Basic familiarity with Markdown (helpful but not required)

::: {.notes}
Make sure everyone has Quarto installed before starting.
:::

# Session 1: Getting Started {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## What is Quarto?

::: {.incremental}
- **Next-generation** scientific and technical publishing system
- Works with R, Python, Julia, and Observable JS
- Creates documents, presentations, websites, books, and more
- **One source → multiple outputs** (HTML, PDF, Word, slides)
- Open source and developed by Posit (formerly RStudio)
:::

::: {.fragment}
Think of it as: **Markdown + Code + Output = Beautiful Documents**
:::

## Why Quarto?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Advantages:**

- Reproducible research
- Multiple output formats
- Language agnostic
- Active community
- Easy to learn
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Use Cases:**

- Research papers
- Reports & dashboards
- Presentations
- Websites & blogs
- Books & tutorials
:::
:::

## Your First Quarto Document

**File structure:**

```markdown
---
title: "My First Document"
author: "Your Name"
format: html
---

# Introduction

This is my first Quarto document!

## Section 1

Here's some text with **bold** and *italic*.
```

## YAML Header {.smaller}

The YAML header controls document settings:

```yaml
---
title: "Document Title"
author: "Author Name"
date: "2024-11-19"
format: 
  html:
    toc: true
    code-fold: true
    theme: cosmo
---
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Pro Tip
YAML is indentation-sensitive! Use spaces, not tabs.
:::

## Markdown Basics

```markdown
# Heading 1
## Heading 2
### Heading 3

**bold text**
*italic text*
~~strikethrough~~

- Bullet point
- Another point
  - Nested point

1. Numbered list
2. Second item
```

## Exercise 1: Create Your First Document {background-color="#097969"}

**Task (5 minutes):**

1. Open RStudio or VS Code
2. Create a new Quarto document (`.qmd`)
3. Add a YAML header with title, author, and format
4. Write a brief introduction about yourself
5. Add at least 2 sections with headings
6. Use bold, italic, and a list
7. Render the document (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K)

::: {.fragment}
**Bonus:** Try changing the format to `pdf` or `docx`
:::

## Working with Code Chunks

**R example:**

````markdown
```{{r}}
# This is an R code chunk
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
mean(x)
```
````

**Python example:**

````markdown
```{{python}}
# This is a Python code chunk
numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(f"Mean: {sum(numbers)/len(numbers)}")
```
````

## Code Chunk Options {.smaller}

Control how code appears:

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| echo: false      # Hide code, show output
#| eval: true       # Run the code
#| warning: false   # Hide warnings
#| message: false   # Hide messages
#| fig-cap: "My Plot"

plot(cars)
```
````

::: {.callout-note}
Use `#|` for chunk options (recommended) or `{r, echo=FALSE}` style
:::

## Inline Code

Mix code with text:

```markdown
The mean of our data is `r mean(c(1,2,3,4,5))`.

We analyzed `python len(data)` observations.
```

Output:

The mean of our data is 3.

We analyzed 150 observations.

## Exercise 2: Add Code to Your Document {background-color="#097969"}

**Task (8 minutes):**

1. Add a code chunk that creates a simple calculation
2. Create a visualization (scatter plot, bar chart, etc.)
3. Use `#| echo: false` to hide the code for one chunk
4. Add inline code to reference a calculated value
5. Render and check the output

::: {.fragment}
**Bonus:** Try `#| code-fold: true` to make code collapsible
:::

## Creating Tables

**Markdown tables:**

```markdown
| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| A        | B        | C        |
| 1        | 2        | 3        |
```

**From code:**

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| label: tbl-example
#| tbl-cap: "Sample Data"

library(knitr)
kable(head(mtcars, 5))
```
````

## Images and Figures

**Markdown syntax:**

```markdown
![Caption text](path/to/image.png)

![Logo](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){width=50%}
```

**From code:**

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| label: fig-plot
#| fig-cap: "Scatter plot of cars data"

plot(cars)
```
````

## Cross-References {.smaller}

Reference figures, tables, and sections:

```markdown
See @fig-plot for the visualization.

As shown in @tbl-example, the data includes...

More details in @sec-methods.

# Methods {#sec-methods}
```

::: {.callout-important}
Labels must start with `fig-`, `tbl-`, or `sec-` for auto-numbering
:::

# Session 2: Advanced Features {background-color="#2C5F2D"}

## Callout Blocks

Create attention-grabbing blocks:

```markdown
::: {.callout-note}
This is a note callout.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
This is a warning!
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Custom Title
Pro tips go here!
:::
```

Types: `note`, `warning`, `important`, `tip`, `caution`

## Divs and Spans

**Divs** for blocks:

```markdown
::: {.class-name}
Content here
:::

::: {style="background-color: lightblue; padding: 10px;"}
Custom styled content
:::
```

**Spans** for inline:

```markdown
This is [special text]{.highlight}.

This is [red text]{style="color: red;"}.
```

## Layouts and Columns {.smaller}

**Two-column layout:**

```markdown
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
Left column content
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
Right column content
:::
:::
```

**Multiple panels:**

```markdown
::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Image 1](img1.png)

![Image 2](img2.png)
:::
```

## Tabsets

Create tabbed content:

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

## Tab 1
Content for tab 1

## Tab 2  
Content for tab 2

## Tab 3
Content for tab 3

:::
```

## Exercise 4: Formatting & Layout {background-color="#097969"}

**Task (10 minutes):**

1. Add at least 2 different callout blocks
2. Create a two-column layout
3. Add a custom styled div
4. Create tabbed content with 3 tabs
5. Experiment with different styles

## Citations and Bibliography {.smaller}

**Add bibliography to YAML:**

```yaml
---
title: "My Research"
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl  # Optional: citation style
---
```

**Cite in text:**

```markdown
As shown by @smith2020, the results are significant.

Multiple sources [@jones2019; @smith2020].

See [Chapter 3, @doe2021] for details.
```

::: {.callout-note}
References will auto-generate at the end
:::

## Creating Presentations

**RevealJS slides:**

```yaml
---
title: "My Presentation"
format: 
  revealjs:
    theme: dark
    slide-number: true
    chalkboard: true
---

## Slide 1

Content here

## Slide 2

More content
```

## Presentation Features {.smaller}

**Incremental lists:**

```markdown
::: {.incremental}
- Point 1
- Point 2
- Point 3
:::
```

**Fragments:**

```markdown
::: {.fragment}
This appears on click
:::
```

**Speaker notes:**

```markdown
::: {.notes}
Notes only you can see
:::
```

## Advanced Presentation Layouts {.smaller}

**Background images:**

```markdown
## {background-image="image.jpg"}

## {background-color="#43464B"}
```

**Centered content:**

```markdown
## {.center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
Large centered text!
:::
```

**Absolute positioning:**

```markdown
::: {.absolute top=200 left=50}
Positioned content
:::
```

## Multiple Output Formats

**Single source, multiple formats:**

```yaml
---
title: "Flexible Document"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    theme: cosmo
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
  docx:
    reference-doc: template.docx
---
```

Render specific format: `quarto render doc.qmd --to pdf`

## Parameterized Reports {.smaller}

**Add parameters:**

```yaml
---
title: "Sales Report"
params:
  region: "North"
  year: 2024
---
```

**Use in code:**

````markdown
```{{r}}
region <- params$region
year <- params$year

# Filter data based on parameters
filtered_data <- data %>% 
  filter(Region == region, Year == year)
```
````

Render with params: `quarto render report.qmd -P region:South`

## Publishing Your Work {.smaller}

**Quarto Pub (free):**

```bash
quarto publish quarto-pub document.qmd
```

**GitHub Pages:**

```bash
quarto publish gh-pages
```

**Other options:**

- Netlify
- Posit Connect
- Confluence
- Custom server

## Quarto Projects {.smaller}

**Create a project:**

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My Website"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - about.qmd
```

**Project types:**

- `website` - Personal or project website
- `book` - Long-form documentation
- `manuscript` - Academic manuscripts

## Common Issues & Solutions {.smaller}

**YAML errors:**

- Check indentation (use spaces!)
- Ensure colons have spaces after them
- Validate YAML syntax

**Rendering fails:**

- Check code chunk syntax
- Look for missing packages
- Review error messages carefully

**Formatting issues:**

- Try clearing cache: `quarto render --cache-refresh`
- Check for conflicting CSS/LaTeX

## Tips for Success

::: {.incremental}
1. **Start simple** - Master basics before advanced features
2. **Use templates** - Learn from existing examples
3. **Read error messages** - They're usually helpful!
4. **Experiment** - Try new features in test documents
5. **Check the docs** - Quarto documentation is excellent
6. **Join the community** - Ask questions, share work
:::

## Bonus: Keyboard Shortcuts

**RStudio:**

- Render: `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`
- Insert chunk: `Ctrl/Cmd + Alt/Option + I`
- Run chunk: `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Enter`

**VS Code:**

- Render: `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`
- Preview: `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + V`

## Bonus: YAML Templates {.smaller}

**HTML Document:**

```yaml
---
title: "Report"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    embed-resources: true
    theme: cosmo
---
```

**PDF Document:**

```yaml
---
title: "Article"
format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: article
    geometry: margin=1in
    number-sections: true
---
```
